provenance: Questions in this file were adopted from the MIT-licensed project Onesayi/ccna-simulator at commit 6efca4f15e8ccf01fb44973b46bb26922797965a (Alistair Nhiwatiwa, 2026-10-04), originally authored against the CCNA v1.0 blueprint and re-keyed here to the v1.1 leaf objective IDs in src/data/objectives.json. The full per-question mapping, including every item dropped as out of scope and the reason, is in docs/ADOPTED.md. Each question records its origin in its `upstream` field. Distractor rationales are marked TODO and are written during Phase 2; no question ships without them.

questions.prompt: What sets an agentic AI system apart from a generative AI chatbot in network operations?

A.text: It replaces routing protocols with machine learning
A.rationale: TODO: explain why this is wrong

B.text: It needs no permissions because it only reads data
B.rationale: TODO: explain why this is wrong

C.text: It can plan multi-step tasks and act on them with tools, such as running show commands, toward a goal

D.text: It only answers questions in natural language
D.rationale: TODO: explain why this is wrong

questions.explanation: An agent pursues a goal by choosing and calling tools in a loop. Because it can act, it needs scoped permissions and human oversight.

questions.prompt: An AI agent diagnoses an outage and proposes a configuration change on a production core switch. What is the sound practice?

A.text: Apply it, then ask the agent to check its own work
A.rationale: TODO: explain why this is wrong

B.text: Ignore the proposal; AI output is never useful
B.rationale: TODO: explain why this is wrong

C.text: Review and approve the change, and its rollback, before it is applied

D.text: Let the agent apply it at once, since it found the fault
D.rationale: TODO: explain why this is wrong

questions.explanation: Agents speed up diagnosis, but changes to production need a human in the loop, validation against the evidence and a way back.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Ansible is true?

A.text: It needs an agent installed on every router
A.rationale: TODO: explain why this is wrong

B.text: Devices pull their configuration from it on a schedule
B.rationale: TODO: explain why this is wrong

C.text: Its playbooks are written in Ruby
C.rationale: TODO: explain why this is wrong

D.text: It is agentless and pushes changes over SSH using YAML playbooks

questions.explanation: Ansible needs only SSH (or an API) on the managed device. Puppet and Chef traditionally use agents and a pull model.
